title: Ethiopian Tropical Fruit Platter
community: All of Ethiopia — the fruit abundance of the highlands and lowlands
author: Mama Tigist
desc: Ethiopian Tropical Fruit Platter — a generous arrangement of Ethiopia's finest fruits: mango, papaya, banana, avocado, guava, passion fruit, and watermelon, dressed with a honey-lemon-cardamom syrup. Ethiopia's remarkable fruit diversity on one beautiful plate.
longDesc: Ethiopia's fruit diversity is extraordinary — from the mango of the lowlands to the highland strawberries of Jimma, from the papaya of the Rift Valley to the avocado of the highland gardens. The fruit platter celebrates this diversity with a simple honey-cardamom dressing that enhances without overpowering.
ingredients: // Selection of Ethiopian fruits (use what is available):
steps: Mix honey, lemon juice, and cardamom for the dressing.
Prepare all fruits — peel and slice where needed.
Arrange on a large plate artfully — no rules, only abundance.
Place passion fruit halves for guests to squeeze themselves.
chefTips: The avocado is typically not served in sweet fruit platters internationally — in Ethiopia it absolutely is.
Passion fruit is squeezed over everything by guests — provide half fruits not pulp.
Ethiopian mango (Tommy Atkins or Kent) at peak ripeness requires no dressing — but the honey-cardamom elevates everything.
commonMistakes: Preparing too far ahead — avocado and banana discolour.
cookingScience: The lemon juice in the dressing inhibits enzymatic browning on avocado and banana. The honey's hygroscopic properties draw the fruit's own juices to the surface, creating a natural additional dressing.
sustainabilityTips: Ethiopian highland and lowland fruits — grown within the country at every altitude from Rift Valley lowlands to Jimma highlands.
servedWith: As a light conclusion to rich Ethiopian meals
healthBenefits: Extraordinary vitamin C from guava and passion fruit.
Very high antioxidant diversity from multiple fruits.
culturalNote: The Ethiopian fruit platter is the dessert that requires no cooking and no complexity — just the extraordinary diversity of Ethiopian fruits arranged with care and dressed with the country's finest honey. It is Ethiopia's agricultural abundance made edible.
